As a young woman farming a small rented plot in Kagera, I must be careful with my limited money because this land is not my own. Beans fix nitrogen in the soil, so I will save my money and not buy costly chemical fertilizer, but I will spread manure from our family livestock to help the crops grow. I will plant seeds I saved from last season and rely on the rains, since I cannot afford irrigation pipes or pumps for land I do not own. My family and I will do all the work ourselves—planting, weeding, and harvesting—because hiring labor is too expensive for such a small plot.
